name: Mondzi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Endo, Mitsuaki (ed.). 2017. Studies in Asian Geolinguistics VII: Tone and Accent. Tokyo: ILCAA. https://publication.aa-ken.jp/sag7_tone_2017.pdf
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Typological survey: Lolo-Burmese languages typed generically as 'A-1 Syllable tone'; Mondzi/Mondzish not named. Generic second-hand only.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2017. Mondzish lexical database (xlsx). Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.1249169
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lexical database with a 'Mondzi [Lama 2012]' column; string search for stress/accent finds nothing; cites Lu Zhengyuan & Nong Lansheng (eds) 1998 Funing Xian Minzu Zhi for ethnic subgroup names (Black/White/Flowery Yi of Funing).

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. n.d. [2017-2018]. MSEA Languages website, 'Mondzish branch' and 'Munji' pages. https://sites.google.com/site/msealangs/mondzish-branch
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Classification (Munji/Mantsi cluster = Southern Mondzish) and field-note pages; no Mondzi page; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2014. Mondzish: a new subgroup of Lolo-Burmese. Proceedings of the 14th International Symposium on Chinese Languages and Linguistics (IsCLL-14), 62-81. Taipei: Academia Sinica (+ presentation slides). Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.1127814
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Classification and comparative lexicon only. Mondzi ('Monji') is entered as 'mo²¹nʥi²¹, Musang, Daping Village, Muyang Township, Funing County, ~2,000?, YYFC (1983) quoted in Ziwo Lama (2012)'; Table 5 compares Mongi/Mondzi/Munji forms with syllable tones. No phonology section; the words stress/accent do not occur.

sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) languages: a study from the perspectives of shared innovation and phylogenetic estimation. PhD diss., University of Texas at Arlington. hdl.handle.net/10106/11161
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: Printed p.84 (PDF p.103) sketch: 'Mondzi [mo21ndʑi21] is spoken in Funing County, Yunnan and in Hà Giang province, Vietnam.. Mondzi has 40 initials, 27 vowels (11 monophthongs and 13 diphthongs), 6 tones (/55/, /44/, /33/, /53/, /13/, and /21/) (cf. YYFC 1983).' Tone table (PDF p.126) repeats the six tones. The words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur anywhere in the dissertation; nothing on prominence. Data from YYFC 1983 handwritten ms., Musang, Daping Village, Muyang Township, Funing.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Mondzi language' (redirect to 'Mantsi language') and 'Mondzish languages'; Wikidata Q16919822
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mantsi article reproduces Lama 2012's Mondzi consonant/vowel/tone inventory; no mention of stress. References cited: Edmondson 2003, Hsiu 2014, Lama 2012, Iwasa 2003 (Ma Ndzi = Black Lolo of Cao Bang, Vietnam, i.e. mant1265 not mond1267).

sources.citation: Wu Zili 武自立. 1993. 云南富宁末昂话初探 [A preliminary study of the Mo'ang language of Funing, Yunnan]. Minzu Yuwen 1993(2): 53-63
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: Nearest published phonological sketch of a Mondzish language in the same county (Maang/Mo'ang, maan1239 — a sister language, not Mondzi); would give only comparative evidence on Mondzish prosody.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2022. The phonetic tone change *high > rising: evidence from the Ngwi dialect laboratory. Diachronica 39(2): 226-267 (+ Zenodo 4643782 Appendices_1_2_3.xlsx)

sources.note: Only refereed phonological study that uses Mondzi (mond1267) data; concerns lexical tone change, so at most it would confirm the six-tone inventory and prosodic typing, not a stress rule. Full text paywalled

sources.citation: Zhang Tingxian 张廷仙 (ed.). 2017. 云南彝语方言词语汇编 [Yunnan Yiyu fangyan ciyu huibian / Compilation of Yunnan Yi dialect vocabulary]. (Glottolog ref 669327; listed by Glottolog as a wordlist; section 'Funing Mondzi')
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Published version of the 1983 YYFC Yi-dialect vocabulary that is the sole primary data source for Mondzi; Chinese vocabulary compilations of this type usually open each lect with initials/finals/tones and occasionally a note on syllable prominence. Glottolog holds a scan (jsondata fn) but it is not online.
